transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Name]. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Um… yeah. I came in because I can’t seem to stop focusing on my face, specifically the left side. It looks uneven and kind of puffy to me, especially on video calls, which is awkward because I work in computer support and I’m on calls a lot. And then I do salsa, or I used to enjoy it more, and in photos from that I just… I zoom in and it’s all I can see.

People keep telling me they don’t notice anything, like, “You look fine,” but that almost makes it more frustrating because I feel like I’m staring at something obvious. It’s starting to affect work and my social life, which sounds a little ridiculous when I say it out loud, but it’s been hard to shake.
Do you find yourself doing anything repeatedly, like checking mirrors, taking certain photos, or trying to fix the way your face looks in some way?

Yeah… I do. I mean, before a meeting I’ll open the camera preview just to “check,” but then I’m moving the laptop around, trying different lighting, turning my face, seeing if the left side looks worse. And then I’ll start fixing my hair over that side, like maybe if it sits a certain way it won’t be so noticeable.

It’s the same if I’m going out. I’ll take a picture, hate it, retake it from a different angle, and then somehow twenty minutes are gone. Sometimes I ask my friends, like, “Do I look weird?” or “Is my face uneven?” and they’ll say no, but I don’t really feel reassured. I just keep asking, which I know is probably annoying.

I’ve definitely made myself late doing it. Or I get so worn out from trying to look… normal, I guess, that I don’t even want to go anymore.

How much do these concerns about your face bother you when you're not actively checking or trying to fix things? Like, can you put it out of your mind, or does it kind of hang there in the background?

It kind of hangs there, yeah. Like even if I’m not actively checking, I’m still aware of it, if that makes sense. I’ll be working and then a video call will pop up, and I’m thinking about the left side of my face before I’m even thinking about what the person is asking me.

And then with salsa—sorry, this is maybe not exactly what you asked—but people take photos after class or at socials, and I’ll try to act normal, but part of me is already worried about how my face is going to look in the picture. The unevenness, or like it looks puffy on that side. Everyone says they don’t see it, which I know should help, but it doesn’t really. It just stays in the back of my mind and makes work and social stuff feel harder than it should.
Have these concerns about your face ever caused you to avoid certain situations, or made it hard for you to function at work or in your personal life?

Yeah… it has, unfortunately. At work, I’ve missed some ticket deadlines because I get kind of stuck before or after video calls, like trying to make myself look okay on camera instead of just moving on. And I’ve joined calls late for the same reason, which is embarrassing because I’m supposed to be helping other people with their computer issues, not… fussing with my own camera angle.

My supervisor actually brought it up in a performance review, the lateness and deadlines, not the face thing. I didn’t really explain it properly. I think I just said I’d been having trouble staying on track.

And socially, yeah, I’ve skipped salsa nights and some community events if I knew people would be taking photos. Which is sad because I actually like going. I mean, the music and everything—I used to look forward to it all week. But then if I imagine pictures being posted later, I just decide it’s easier not to go.
Has this concern with your face affected your personal relationships or the way you feel about yourself overall?

Yeah… I think it has. I mean, with relationships it’s not always like a big argument or anything, it’s more that I start pulling back. Like salsa nights—there’s this one place that does socials and everyone takes group pictures at the end, and I used to love that whole thing, the music, seeing familiar people, all of it. But if I know there’ll be photos, I’ll just skip it. Same with community events sometimes.

And with work too, which I know isn’t exactly personal relationships, but it affects how I feel about myself. I’ve missed ticket deadlines and joined video calls late because I couldn’t get past how I looked on camera. My supervisor brought it up in a performance review, and I just felt… really ashamed. Like I’m supposed to be competent, I have a graduate degree, I help other people with their computer problems, and then I’m sitting there stuck on my own face.

So overall, yeah, it makes me feel kind of embarrassed and frustrated with myself. Like I’m letting this thing run parts of my life that should be normal.
